For example, even if the S&P 500 is trading near its highs, if $S5FI and $S5TH are declining, it could mean that only a handful of large-cap stocks are supporting the index while the average stock is already starting to break down.

If you only look at the index, the market may still appear strong, while breakouts in the individual stocks you actually trade are becoming more likely to fail.

That’s why I always keep an eye on which direction $S5FI and $S5TH are moving.
That’s also why I include the $S5TH chart in the market condition update I post every day.

Fri Sep 11 | 6:30 AM CT
SPX event structures in yesterday's book.

Investors now think the likelihood of an FOMC rate high next week, based on August data, is 67%.

Let's look at yesterday's order book to see how institutions are positioning for the announcement .. because yesterday's signed book was full of event structures.

Dominating ... straddles, synthetics, and collars ... clustered around SPX 7595 - 7605.  
A paucity of butterflies and condors.

Big specs:
   •  Long ATM straddles (paying for the move)
Hedging the decision:
   •  $3.4M, five legs (a financed collar with a tail attached, expiring a month after the meeting ... built to survive being wrong).
   •  December collars were rebuilt lower.
Counterflow:
   •  14:29 - 15:14 a program sold hundreds of far OTM (tail) puts in 50-lot clips ... either trimming or harvesting deep protection.

SUMMARY

Both sides trading around the same strike (7600) ... but the premium-weighted flow leans to hedge through the event.  The biggest single structure of the day was insurance.

In other words books are positioned to hold through the meeting, paying up to 1.75% (e.g. the Sep 7595 straddle).  Collar packages and outright put buys outweighed bullish synthetics roughly 2:1.  

Taken together, this is consistent with protecting large long books into year-end.

BTW

This relates to why the APMEM volatility forecast (https://t.co/dF28lKlcx1) remains on chill and why the selloff has remained "orderly" so far.  
Pre-hedged holders don't panic-bid vol.

I don’t constantly feel the need to explain my schedule to strangers on the internet, but since apparently we’re doing a calendar audit, here's what my life actually looks like right now:

Since August, I’ve been in a 10-month Master’s/Fellows program that ends in May.

Monday-Thursday, I work a 9-5 through the program. Fridays are dedicated to classes for my Master’s, and a lot of my weekends involve retreats, community service + leadership development. There are 16 of us Fellows living in the same building, so this isn’t exactly the traditional “go to class twice a week and chill” graduate school experience. It’s intentionally a very full season of my life.

I also trade actively, run businesses, manage an e-commerce brand, and create content.

The part people seem to miss is that being busy doesn’t mean every responsibility requires my attention simultaneously for 12 hours a day. I’ve spent years+ (since I was 16) simplifying and systemizing my trading. I’ve done the same thing with my businesses, automating, delegating, and building systems around repetitive work so my attention can currently be concentrated on my job, Master’s, trading & the things that actually require me.

Is it a lot? Heck yeah, absolutely. I sacrifice a LOT of free time, and I’d argue I’m willing to work harder than 99% of people my age.

I spend an absurd amount of my remaining time reading, writing, studying markets, and working on myself. That isn’t me claiming I’m Superman or that everyone should structure their life this way...it’s simply the season I’ve intentionally chosen, and I think that work ethic has played a pretty meaningful role in putting me in the position I’m fortunate enough to be in at 22.

And this isn’t forever.

The program ends in May, and my plan is to trade full-time afterward.

Until next May, I’m going to keep doing what I’ve always done...simplify, systemize, work my butt off, and focus on my own lane.

You don’t have to believe my schedule “checks out.” Thankfully, my calendar doesn’t require approval from X.

Godspeed, family!

The headline number and the linked prediction market odds now at 80% for a 25bps hike might not paint the full picture. 

Core CPI is the lowest it has been for over a year. 

The BLS says gasoline alone accounted for more than one-third of August’s monthly headline increase. On a 12-month contribution basis:

-Energy contributed approximately 1.08 percentage points of the 3.4% headline number.

-Gasoline alone contributed approximately 0.87 percentage points.

In other words, energy generated roughly 32% of total year-over-year headline inflation, despite representing only 7.3% of the CPI basket. Gasoline alone generated roughly one-quarter of headline inflation. 

Oil is a supply issue, we are looking to raise and are pricing in multiple rate hikes for a momentary issue while the core and rest are near the 2% target!

The biggest edge in the market right now isn’t technicals or fundamentals.

Most people can learn both.

The real edge is something much harder to master:

Discipline + Patience.

I see so many people expecting instant profits. A stock does nothing for a few weeks or months, and suddenly they’re questioning the thesis or chasing whatever is moving that day.

Many great traders and investors spent years developing their process. Why should we expect to master it overnight?

The harder skill is having the discipline to follow your process and the patience to let a good thesis actually play out.

And patience doesn’t mean buying a struggling turnaround and blindly holding it for 10 years.

For me, it means finding profitable businesses growing 20%+ with strong fundamentals, strong technicals and powerful themes then giving those businesses enough time to compound while the thesis remains intact.

Learn the fundamentals. Learn the technicals.

But master patience + discipline.

That’s where the real edge is.
